raw_text:
Below is a complete 12-week, four-days-per-week strength program tailored to a 36-year-old recreational lifter with a prior right medial meniscus tear. Constraints from the surgeon: low-impact, no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load. The plan emphasizes hip hinge and posterior chain work, controlled knee loading, and ski-specific strength without plyometrics or deep-knee flexion under load. It includes phase structure, weekly sessions, exercises, sets/reps, and progression, plus nutrition and recovery guidance.

Important safety notes
- If any knee pain worsens, or you notice sharp pain, swelling, or instability, scale back ROM, reduce weight, or replace the movement with a safer alternative.
-Prioritize technique and knee-friendly ROM over loading. Stop any set if pain or wobble occurs.
-Consult the client’s surgeon or a PT if there is any concern about a specific movement.

Overall structure
- Phase 1: Foundation and tolerance building (Weeks 1–4). Establish correct mechanics, light loads, and knee-friendly ROM. Deload in Week 4.
- Phase 2: Strength development and progressive overload (Weeks 5–8). Increase intensity with comparable ROM, add unilateral work, and tighten technique.
- Phase 3: Peak strength and ski-readiness (Weeks 9–12). Peak strength work with lower volume but higher intensity; add ski-specific stability and anti-rotation work; finalize readiness for skiing next season.

Weekly framework (4 sessions per week)
- Day A: Lower body – hip hinge/posterior chain emphasis (no jumping)
- Day B: Upper body – push
- Day C: Lower body – quad-friendly, controlled ROM (no deep knee flexion under load)
- Day D: Upper body – pull

All main lifts are performed with a ROM that stays within the knee’s safe limits (generally: up to roughly parallel or shallower for squats, controlled knee bend not exceeding comfort level; no deep knee flexion under load). If a given movement cannot be performed safely, substitute with a knee-friendly alternative.

Week-by-week plan (weeks 1–12)

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation and tolerance)
Week 1
- Day A (Lower – hinge emphasis)
  • Romanian Deadlift (RDL) 3x8
  • Barbell Hip Thrust or Dumbbell Hip Bridge 3x10
  • Leg Press (ROM to ~90° knee bend) 3x12
  • Split Squat (step length minimized; shallow ROM) 3x8 per leg
  • Standing Calf Raise 3x15
  • Core: Pallof Press or dead bug 3x10 per side
- Day B (Upper – push)
  • Bench Press or Dumbbell Bench 4x6–8
  • Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press 3x8
  • One-Arm Dumbbell Row or Dumbbell Row 3x8
  • Lat Pulldown 3x8
  • Dumbbell Lateral Raise 3x12
  • Triceps Pushdown 3x12
- Day C (Lower – quad-friendly)
  • Goblet Squat to parallel (or to comfortable ROM) 3x8
  • Reverse Lunges (short step, ROM controlled) 3x8 per leg
  • Lying Hamstring Curl 3x10
  • Cable Hip Abduction/Adduction 2x12 each side
  • Calf Raise 3x15
- Day D (Upper – pull)
  • Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-Up 4x6–8
  • Barbell or Dumbbell Row 3x8
  • Seated Cable Row 3x10
  • Face Pull 3x12
  • Bicep Curl 3x10
  • Farmer’s Carry 2x30s

Week 2
- Rep scheme same as Week 1, but aim to add small load or 1 extra rep per set where technique remains clean.
- Ensure ROM remains within knee-safe range.

Week 3
- Similar structure. Increase weight slightly (2.5–5%), keep reps in the same band. Emphasize tempo: 2-0-1 for squats and 3-0-1 for hip hinge if comfortable.

Week 4 (Deload)
- Reduce volume to about 60% of Week 3 loads and cut sets by 1 per exercise.
- Tempo: controlled, no forced reps.
- Keep ROM comfortable and technique sharp.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Strength development)
Week 5
- Day A (Lower – posterior chain focus)
  • Barbell RDL 4x6
  • Hip Thrust 4x8
  • Leg Press 3x10 (ROM to 90°)
  • Step-Ups or Elevated Split Squat (short ROM) 3x8 per leg
  • Standing Calf Raise 4x12
  • Pallof Press 3x12 per side
- Day B (Upper – push)
  • Bench Press 4x6
  • Overhead Press 4x6
  • Bent-Over DB Row 3x8
  • Incline Dumbbell Row 3x8
  • Lateral Raise 3x12
  • Tricep Rope Pushdown 3x12
- Day C (Lower – quad-friendly emphasis)
  • Goblet Squat to parallel 4x6
  • Reverse Lunges (short ROM) 3x6 per leg
  • Hamstring Curl 3x12
  • Cable Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge 3x12
  • Calf Raise 4x12
- Day D (Upper – pull)
  • Weighted Pull-Up or Lat Pulldown 4x6–8
  • Cable Face Pull 3x12
  • Barbell or Dumbbell Row 3x8
  • Seated Row 3x10
  • Bicep Curl 3x12

Week 6
- Increase weight modestly on main lifts if technique remains solid. Maintain ROM limits.

Week 7
- Add a tempo element on one main lift per day (e.g., 3 seconds lowering, 1 second pause, fast up) to increase time under tension while keeping knee loading reasonable.
- Keep accessory weights conservative.

Week 8 (Deload)
- Similar to Week 4: reduce volume and loads to ~60–70% with a focus on technique and recovery.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Peak strength and ski-readiness)
Week 9
- Day A (Lower – hinge/heavy)
  • Barbell RDL 5x4–5
  • Hip Thrust 4x6
  • Leg Press 3x8 (ROM to 90°)
  • Step-Ups or Loaded Split Squats 3x6 per leg
  • Calf Raise 4x12
  • Anti-Rotation Core (Pallof press) 3x12 per side
- Day B (Upper – push)
  • Bench Press 5x4–6
  • Overhead Press 4x4–6
  • Bent-Over Row 4x6
  • Incline Dumbbell Press 3x6–8
  • Face Pull 3x12
- Day C (Lower – quad-friendly peak)
  • Front Squat to parallel or shallow ROM (if tolerated) 4x5
  • Reverse Lunges with short ROM 3x5 per leg
  • Hamstring Curl 3x8
  • Glute Bridge or Hip Thrust 3x6
  • Calf Raise 4x12
- Day D (Upper – pull)
  • Weighted Pull-Up or Lat Pulldown 4x6
  • T-bar Row or Barbell Row 4x6
  • Seated Cable Row 3x8
  • Rear Deltoid Fly 3x12
  • Bicep Curl 3x10

Week 10
- Maintain Week 9 intensity but ensure technique holds. If any lift is lagging, adjust to stay within knee safety ROM.

Week 11
- Lift variety with a slight decrease in volume to prepare for testing. Maintain intensity or attempt a light lighter triple on main lifts for confidence.

Week 12
- Performance test and ski readiness check. Focus on stable technique and controlled movements rather than maximal loads.
  • Optional: 1RM estimate or 3–5RM attempts on safe lifts (e.g., bench, RDL, leg press) if knee tolerates it.
  • Ski-specific readiness: incorporate 2–3 sets of lateral band walks (with light resistance), single-leg balance progression (eyes closed on stable surface), and controlled hip hinge and anti-rotation patterns.

Program progression notes
- Progression strategy: aim for small weekly increases (2.5–5% on main lifts) or add a set or a couple of reps if technique is solid and knee symptoms are minimal.
- If knee pain increases with a given movement, switch to a knee-friendly alternative for that week (e.g., replace a challenging lunge with a shallow step-up; replace a deep squat with a controlled goblet squat to parallel).
- Use a rate of perceived exertion (RPE) target of 7–8 for the main lifts in Weeks 1–4, 7–8 for Weeks 5–8, and 8–9 for Weeks 9–12, adjusting to stay within knee safety constraints.
- When testing, focus on movement quality and consistency rather than maximum weight.

Conditioning and mobility
- 2–3 light cardio sessions per week (20–30 minutes) of low-impact activity (e.g., cycling, rowing, swimming) to support conditioning without joint overload.
- Mobility work daily: hips, ankles, and thoracic spine; include hip flexor/quad releases, hamstring mobility, ankle dorsiflexion, and thoracic mobility.
- Post-workout: 5–10 minutes of gentle cooling and mobility or light foam rolling (hamstrings, glutes, calves, mid-back).

Sample ski-specific conditioning additions (optional)
- Lateral band walks: 2–3 sets of 12–15 steps per side, 1–2x/week
- Single-leg stability work: cossack-style balance with light loads, 2–3 sets of 20–30 seconds per leg
- Anti-rotation holds: Pallof press 3x12 per side
- Controlled lateral lunges with shallow ROM and emphasis on knee tracking over toes

Nutrition and recovery guidelines
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day to support muscle repair and growth. Distribute evenly across meals.
- Total calories: aim for a modest surplus (about 250–500 kcal/day) if weight gain is desired and knee tolerance is stable, or maintain current weight if leaning toward recovery and ski readiness without mass gain.
- Timing: 20–40 g protein within 1–2 hours after training; carbohydrate intake around workouts to support training energy.
- Hydration: aim for 2–3 liters of fluid per day (adjust for body weight and climate).
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night for recovery.
- Supplements (optional): Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g daily; consider vitamin D if deficient, omega-3s if not regularly consumed; consult a clinician before starting any supplement.

Monitoring and adjustments
- Use knee symptoms as a guide: ROM and load adjustments may be necessary as you progress.
- If pain arises during a lift, reduce ROM or weight or substitute the movement for that week.
- Have a weekly check-in to assess progress, knee comfort, and ski-readiness notes. If skiing will resume during the training window, tailor the last 2–3 weeks toward ski-specific movements and endurance.

Delivery format notes
- The plan is designed for a gym with standard equipment (barbell, dumbbells, machines, cable machines). If any equipment isn’t available, I can substitute with equivalent movements.
- If you want more specificity (e.g., exact order of lifts, exact warm-up), I can provide a ready-to-use one-page template per week with exact warm-up sets and progression targets.

This plan balances strength development with the knee protection required by the meniscal tear, while building toward a safer, stronger return to skiing next season. If you’d like, I can tailor the exact loads (starting 1RM estimates or approximate loads) to the client’s current numbers and adjust the ROM caps for each movement based on his latest knee-friendly range.
